Present:- Mr. Parminder Singh,
Advocate, for the petitioner.

Harnaresh Singh Gill, J. (Qral)
1.
Through this petition, the petitioner seeks anticipatory bail in case bearing FIR No.88 dated 13.03.2023, registered at Police Station Taraori, District Karnal, under Sections 406, 420 and 120-B IPC.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner contends that though the petitioner has falsely been implicated in the present case, yet to show his bona fide, he has issued two cheques bearing Nos.510249 and 510250 dated 25.05.2022, amounting to Rs.21,70,000/-, in total, in favour of the complainant.

3. Notice of motion.
4.

On the asking of this Court, Mr. Rupinder Singh Jhand, Addl.
A. G. Haryana, accepts notice on behalf of the respondent-State.
5. At this stage, Mr. Bhag Singh, Advocate, puts in appearance and files his power of attorney on behalf of the complainant, which is taken on record.

sentences.text: Learned State counsel and learned counsel for the complainant submit that the complainant is the sole proprietor of M/s R.K.Enterprises, which is running a petrol pump; that the petitioner was employed as a Manager of the petrol pump, and that instead of depositing the entire sale proceedings of the pump in the bank account of the firm, the petitioner had embezzled the amount of the complainant to the tune of Rs.21,70,000/-.

It is further submitted that even the petitioner admitted his guilt, vide hand- written note dated 17.05.2022, in the presence of his relatives; that to make up the loss caused to the complainant, the petitioner issued two cheques in favour of the complainant/firm with an assurance that in case, the same were not got encashed, he would be liable to face legal proceedings, and that when both the cheques presented for encashment, the same had got dishonoured.
It is further submitted that recovery is yet to be effected from the petitioner.
7. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties.

8. As per the prosecution version, the petitioner had embezzled an amount of Rs.21,70,000/-
belonging to the complainant/firm.
Even vide hand-written note dated 17.05.2022, the petitioner admitted that he had embezzled the amount and in discharge of his liability, he had issued two cheques, amounting to Rs.21,70,000/-.

However when the same were presented for encashment,
the same had been got dishonoured.

9. Keeping in view the nature and gravity of the offence, this Court finds that to unearth the modus operandi of cheating as also to ascertain the complicity of any other person involved in the commission of the offence, the petitioner is required for custodial interrogation.
| attest to the accuracy and authenticity of this order/judgment 2023: PHHC:094410 CRM-M-34895-2023 10.
In view of the above, this Court does not find any merit in the present petition.

11. Dismissed.
21.07.2023 (HARNARESH SINGH GILL)
